A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same empirical investigation of pre-trained model selection for OOD generalization and calibration. The text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched despite substantial expansion and reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original fine-tuning experiments measuring OOD accuracy and calibration on PACS, VLCS, OfficeHome, and DomainNet, including model-size and pre-training-data comparisons.

after.justification: V2 reports original results for an expanded 97-model investigation, including training-recipe comparisons, optimizer and regularization analyses, robustness-transfer analyses, and repeated-seed accuracy results.

M1.justification: Both versions investigate existing pre-trained classifiers using ERM fine-tuning and training-domain validation for model selection. V2 introduces no new proposed architecture, loss, or algorithm; its additional recipes and optimizers are experimental comparisons.

E1.justification: The four downstream datasets remain. V2 additionally uses JFT-300M-pretrained EfficientNets and evaluates relationships involving ImageNet-A, ImageNet-R, ImageNet-v2, and ImageNet-Real (Section 6.3; Figures B.12–B.13). V1 mentioned some ImageNet robustness resources but reported no corresponding analyses.

E2.justification: V2 substantially expands the evaluated comparison set beyond v1's ResNet, ConvNeXt, and ViT models. Added families include EfficientNet, RegNet, VGG, and MLP-Mixer, alongside distinct pre-training approaches such as DINO, MAE, SAM, AdvProp, and Noisy Student (Table A.1; Figures 6–7 and B.5–B.10).

E3.justification: V1 fixes weight decay at 0.0001 and uses model-dependent learning-rate grids. V2 searches three weight-decay values, broadens learning-rate searches, and compares adaptive optimizers with momentum SGD. The VLCS held-out domain changes from LabelMe to VOC2007 (v1 Appendix B; v2 Table 2). Batch size 32 and 5,000 training iterations remain.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained size, architecture, and ImageNet-accuracy analyses, v2 adds focused investigations of pre-training recipes, supervised versus self-supervised learning, SAM, fine-tuning optimizers, weight decay, validation-based selection, and robustness-to-domain-transfer relationships (Sections 5.3–6; Appendices A–B). These test substantial new questions.

E5.justification: V1 provides no run-count or variability reporting. V2 newly reports three random seeds and presents mean and standard deviation of validation and OOD accuracy for seven selected models across four datasets (Appendix A.3; Table A.2). This is a focused uncertainty check; an increase over v1's unknown run count is not established.

E6.justification: V2 adds extensive accuracy and calibration results for new models, recipes, and sensitivity analyses. Table 1 revises best-model accuracy from 96.8 to 96.7 on PACS, 87.5 to 87.4 on OfficeHome, and 78.2 to 77.8 on DomainNet. VLCS changes from 67.1 to 82.2 alongside a different test domain and selected ViT size. Expanded tuning prevents interpreting these as same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: V2's equations (1)–(3) spell out standard ECE, accuracy, and confidence formulas for the metric already used in v1. Its scaling-law discussion remains empirical interpretation. No new theorem, proof, substantive formal assumption, or mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: V2 retains the claim that pre-trained model choice can matter more than algorithm changes. It adds generic pre-training strategies versus ImageNet-specialized recipes as a central contribution, and explicitly positions improved calibration with larger pre-trained models against earlier observations about poorly calibrated deep networks (Abstract, Contributions, and Section 7).

C2.justification: V2 adds low-accuracy ECE caveats, explanations involving ImageNet overfitting, and dataset-dependent interpretations of regularization. Much of v1's memorization discussion and explicit limitations paragraph is replaced by computational constraints and transfer-aware pre-training directions. Its stronger weight-decay/calibration interpretation in Section 6.2 is qualified by Appendix B.11's statement that clear trends cannot be found.

D1.justification: V2 substantially revises technical documentation with expanded fine-tuning grids, architecture-specific optimizer choices, an annotated model-and-recipe inventory, a study-specific code link, and reported expenditure exceeding 100,000 GPU hours. However, v1's explicit timm checkpoint-identifier mapping in Table A2 is absent from v2's descriptive model table. The code link's availability is not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands research positioning around prior model-selection studies, OOD benchmarks, pre-training recipes, and calibration. Section 3 adds detailed comparisons with earlier studies' model coverage and discusses links between calibration and invariant risk minimization; the calibration results are newly contrasted with Guo et al. This exceeds simply moving v1's related-work appendix.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contributions, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. V1's compact experiment narrative becomes separate Experimental Setup, Results, and Other Findings sections. Related work moves into the main text and is rewritten, while the appendices are reorganized into detailed settings and additional results.

P2.justification: V1's introductory bar chart is replaced by accuracy–calibration scatter plots. Scaling and correlation figures are extensively redrawn with expanded legends, logarithmic parameter axes, and pre-training image-count axes. The model inventory moves into a multi-page appendix table, and numerous recipe, sensitivity, robustness, and uncertainty displays are added.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses important weaknesses of v1's narrow comparison and unexplored optimizer/regularization choices through broader recipe comparisons, targeted sensitivity studies, robustness-transfer analyses, and three-seed checks. These additions substantially strengthen the evidence behind its practical guidance. The missing checkpoint-identifier mapping and inconsistent calibration interpretation, particularly Section 6.2 versus Figure B.11, are drawbacks, but do not outweigh the substantial empirical gains.
